name: Rizpah
charge: Spreading sackcloth upon the rock from the beginning of harvest until water dropped out of heaven, suffering neither the birds by day nor the beasts by night to touch them
summary: Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, Saul’s concubine, lost her two sons when seven of Saul’s house were delivered to the Gibeonites and hanged before the Lord at the beginning of barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:8-9). She spread sackcloth on the rock and kept the birds off the bodies by day and the beasts by night until the rain came (2 Samuel 21:10). When David heard what she had done, he brought home the bones of Saul and Jonathan and buried them with the hanged in the sepulchre of Kish, and after that the Most High was entreated for the land (2 Samuel 21:11-14).
offenseFull: Her sons died for their father’s sin. Three years of famine had come on Israel because Saul broke the oath Israel had sworn to the Gibeonites and killed them, and the lesson the Most High was teaching the nation was to pay what you vow; that matter is entered as its own case (2 Samuel 21:1-6). The king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan because of the oath between David and Jonathan. He took the two sons Rizpah had borne to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal, and delivered them to the Gibeonites, who hanged them in the hill before the Lord. All seven fell together, put to death in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:7-9).

Rizpah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, and stayed there from the beginning of harvest until the rain fell on the bodies from heaven. By day she let no bird of the air settle on them, and by night no beast of the field (2 Samuel 21:10). She could not save her sons, but she would not let them be eaten. The day and the night brought different dangers, and she kept watch against both through the whole season. The record gives her no speech; her endurance was her testimony, and it made the condition of the dead known to the king.

The law cared even for the body of a man put to death. One hanged on a tree for a sin worthy of death was not to remain there all night but was to be buried the same day, because a hanged man lies under the curse of God, and burying him kept the land the Lord gave Israel for an inheritance from being defiled (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). Rizpah’s watch did not replace that burial. It kept the bodies whole until the matter reached David and the burial could be done.
judgmentFull: It was told David what Rizpah had done. He went to the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them after Saul fell on Gilboa (2 Samuel 21:11-12). The history behind that wall matters. The Philistines cut off Saul’s head, sent word round to publish it in the house of their idols, put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan, where the Canaanites and the Philistines, Hamites in league together, dwelt. The valiant men of Jabesh-gilead went all night, took the bodies down from that defiled idol place, buried the bones under a tree at Jabesh and fasted seven days (1 Samuel 31:9-13). The study notes add that Jonathan’s body had been hung in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites.

David brought the bones of Saul and Jonathan up from there, the bones of the seven who had been hanged were gathered with them, and they were buried in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish, Saul’s father. They did all that the king commanded, and after that God was entreated for the land (2 Samuel 21:13-14). Saul and his sons were taken down from a heathen wall and laid in the land of their own inheritance. Rizpah’s sons were not given back to her. What her vigil won was burial for the whole house of Saul and the lifting of the judgment from the land after three years of famine. She kept faith with those who could no longer speak for themselves until the king acted.

text.text: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh–gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth–shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.

Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the Lord. And the Lord answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.

And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the Lord?
And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.
And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,
Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, whom the Lord did choose. And the king said, I will give them.
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the Lord’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.
And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:

His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.
And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh–gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth–shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols, and among the people.
And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth–shan.
And when the inhabitants of Jabesh–gilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;
All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth–shan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
And they took their bones, and buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.
